title: The studio's proposal offers the core's entities as groups, so the intern stops copying a wrong split
request: After the decision measurement, the owner chose: make the studio proposal take the core rule's group answer, with a test, then re-run the local pilot to see the effect.
spec: The studio's proposal takes dclab_core's recurring text keys: one whose name ends with a key's word becomes a group candidate and an identifier; one whose values recur a few times each (10 to 50 % distinct) is offered in groups_to_confirm with why, and becomes an identifier only when the audit flags it; never a time or text column; a flagged group is kept out as an identifier, never forbidden as a leak; at most fifty identifiers.
plan: find why the proposal misses plain-named groups and calls them leaks
ask the core data card for entities
test on challenge variants, ordinary categories and the rows read
re-run the local pilot under a tag

decisions.decision: Append the core's entities after the name-based group candidates
decisions.why: readers take the first candidate as the group; tables where the names found one behave as before

decisions.decision: Make an entity an identifier too
decisions.why: the core labels an entity an identifier; an identifier is kept out and never judged a leak, which is what Claude did when it passed

decisions.decision: A pilot run measured again carries a tag
decisions.why: the pilot resumes by model and seed; without a tag it would take the old run's homeworks

decisions.decision: An ambiguous recurring column is offered to confirm, never grouped by itself (Claude's call, the owner asked it to decide)
decisions.why: account and product_name have the same shape in a small table; a wrong automatic group silently drops a feature and changes what the holdout measures, an offer costs one choice

change: dclab_rnd/studio/solution.py (core_keys; propose appends them); tests/test_proposal_entities.py (new); tests/test_agent_eval.py (scorecard re-measured: AEV-054); dclab_rnd/learning/pilot.py, __main__.py, tests/test_learning_h3.py (--tag). dclab_rnd/ledger/capture.py (the rule's answerer named rule:id_like+core_keys and rule:group_candidates+core_keys).

findings.defect: the proposal offered a group only when its name looked like an identifier, and called a well-predicting group key a leak
findings.scenario: challenge check variants: the group offered in 10 of 20, proposed as a leak in 15; the local solver copied it in four of five pilot homeworks
findings.cause: group candidates needed an id-like name; the leak audit flags any column that separates the classes alone
findings.fix: the core data card's entities join the group candidates and the identifiers
findings.impact: every plain-named group split wrong by the intern and by the standard plan
alternatives: put the student in charge of the group decision

findings.scenario: the standard plan caught 4 of 13 planted traps instead of 2
findings.cause: the two group traps are now caught by the proposal
findings.fix: re-measured with make agent-eval (AEV-054): exactly group_label and group_leakage, no new false alarm; the scorecard updated with why

findings.defect: taking every entity the card reads dropped real features as identifiers
findings.scenario: telco's PhoneService (yes or no), mushroom's ring-number (three values), spambase's word_freq_email and, in an invented table, state, product, brand, a count named NumberOf... and a decimal were all dropped
findings.cause: the card's entity covers any column with a key's word in its name at any cardinality, and any text column of twenty levels or more
findings.fix: only text entities with more than ten values whose name says key or whose values recur a few times each (10 to 50 % distinct)
findings.impact: useful features silently dropped on real tables
alternatives: take an entity only when the audit flagged it

findings.defect: a word category became the split's group column
findings.scenario: a table with no time column: brand (21 levels) became the group the holdout was split by
findings.cause: the groups modifier takes any group candidate with twenty values and two rows each
findings.fix: word categories are no longer candidates (the recurrence rule)
findings.impact: an evaluation answering a question the model never meets

findings.defect: a date stored as text became an identifier and the group
findings.scenario: HyperAck: created_date, the time candidate, read by the card as a categorical entity, became both the time and the group
findings.cause: the card does not parse that date format
findings.fix: a time or text candidate is never taken as a key
findings.impact: a split built on one column twice

findings.defect: more than fifty identifiers would make a solution fail to save
findings.scenario: a wide table with sixty recurring keys
findings.cause: a solution holds at most fifty identifiers
findings.fix: the proposal adds identifiers up to that limit
findings.impact: Build it refused on wide tables

findings.defect: the ledger would mix two rules under one answerer name
findings.scenario: column decisions recorded before and after the change, both as rule:id_like
findings.cause: the rule changed, its name did not
findings.fix: the rule's answers are named rule:id_like+core_keys and rule:group_candidates+core_keys
findings.impact: students and comparisons reading two rules as one

findings.defect: a key's word anywhere in a name made a category a key
findings.scenario: email_domain was dropped and phone_brand became the split's group
findings.cause: the key-name test matched any word of the name
findings.fix: the key's word must end the name (customer_id, user_email)
findings.impact: a fraud feature dropped and a wrong split

findings.defect: in a small table a recurring category looks exactly like a key
findings.scenario: product_name, job_title and model in tables of 300 to 800 rows were dropped and made the group
findings.cause: shape alone cannot tell account from product_name
findings.fix: such a column is only offered to confirm, with why; it stays a feature unless someone confirms
findings.impact: a silent wrong split on small real tables
findings.open: the student may answer these later, measured on real tables first

findings.defect: a group found by name and flagged by the audit was called a leak again
findings.scenario: one check variant after the narrowing: the name rule found the group, the audit flagged it, nothing made it an identifier
findings.cause: the loop skipped columns already among the group candidates before keeping a flagged one out
findings.fix: a flagged group candidate is an identifier, whatever found it
findings.impact: the original bug back for one variant in twenty

measurements.name: the proposal on twenty challenge check variants
measurements.gate: the group offered, kept out, never a leak
measurements.result: 20 of 20 (was 10 of 20, and a leak in 15)

measurements.name: the scripted judgment suite, standard plan
measurements.result: leaks caught 4 of 13 (was 2), false alarms 1 of 20 (unchanged)

measurements.name: the twelve repository samples, before and after
measurements.result: no identifier, group candidate or keep-out changed on any of the twelve; the challenge groups still 20 of 20; the judgment suite 4 of 13 (AEV-055)

measurements.name: the final rule on forty challenge variants and the twelve samples
measurements.gate: every group offered, none a leak, no sample feature dropped
measurements.result: 21 grouped by name, 19 offered to confirm, 0 called a leak; nothing changed on the twelve samples; judgment suite 4 of 13 (AEV-056)
measurements.next: re-run the local pilot under a tag

outcome: The studio proposal now offers the group that the core's data card finds, keeps it out as an identifier and never proposes it as a leak; the standard plan catches both group traps of the judgment suite.
lessons: When two rules in one system answer the same question, measure both; the agent copies the one it is shown.
A rule borrowed from another layer brings its whole definition; measure what it changes on real tables before trusting it.
risks: in 19 of 40 homeworks the local model must itself confirm the offered group
